gap: No result ChatGPT got states that TESmart's own $43.99 2-port HDMI KVM (HKS201-EB23) has EDID emulation and a keyboard/mouse pass-through mode, while UGREEN's manual for the CM664/15707 that ChatGPT showed says it 'does not support Hotkey Switching' and never mentions EDID.
standout_why: I compared this against dockgearhq.com/blog/best-kvm-switches-with-hdmi-2026, deskdna.com/gear/monitors/best-kvm-switch, dockgearhq.com/blog/best-kvm-switches-for-two-computers-one-setup-2026 and officekithq.com/best-kvm-switch-with-hdmi/. Dockgearhq (HDMI) already explains how EDID emulation works, says UGREEN's material 'does not establish the persistent emulation' for the CM664, lists 'no hotkey switching' and warns that emulated keyboard ports reject gaming keyboards. Dockgearhq (two computers) already covers the base M1/M2 limit of one external display. DeskDNA covers EDID only for a DisplayPort TESmart. OfficeKitHQ never mentions EDID. None of them names the TESmart HKS201-EB23 or HKS201-P23, or gives a maker-store price for a 2-PC, 1-monitor HDMI KVM that has EDID emulation. The mechanism itself is not new. Only the product-level pairing of price and mechanism is. I could not open thisusb.com (certificate error).
decides: The shopper wants one monitor shared by two computers without windows rearranging on every switch. EDID emulation decides that, and ChatGPT listed it as a feature without saying which of its cards has it. Its $129.99 card matches TESmart's HKS201-P23, which TESmart says has EDID emulation. The cheapest card, the UGREEN CM664/15707, has no EDID claim I could source from UGREEN. The TESmart HKS201-EB23 costs $43.99 on tesmart.com, less than the UGREEN, and claims EDID emulation, but it is USB 2.0 only. That points to the HKS201-EB23 for basic keyboard and mouse use and the HKS201-P23 if USB 3.0 webcams or drives are shared.
